accessBasis.gate: Home tile showTallySync = !_isRestrictedMember && a business is selected && the business is not the demo company (tally_jobs RLS is company-wide, so the tile is owner-scope).

behaviourReviewed: Four buckets from TallySyncBucket: needsAttention (FAILED/DEAD/stuck), waiting (PENDING/PROCESSING under 48h and any unrecognised status), sent (COMPLETED), noActionNeeded (informational).
kTallySyncStuckAfter = 48 hours; kTallyPullStaleAfter = 24 hours drives the top-line warning colour and the Set up link to /setup-on-pc.
The screen is read-only by design — no retry control exists, because a blind re-push of a partially-landed voucher duplicates it in Tally.
A failed fetch renders Couldn't check the Tally sync with Try again; it never renders as an empty queue.
waitingSubtitle only blames the PC when the pull clock is stale or null; otherwise it stays neutral.
TallySyncExplanations buckets on status, never on error_kind/is_retriable; informational classes (deletion policy, superseded, operator hold) are checked first and stay out of the red count.
COMPLETED reads Sent to Tally, deliberately not 'confirmed in Tally'.
Type filter chips are built only from the types this company actually pushed; an empty filter gets its own message plus Show all.

visibilityBlocked.reason: The screen is gated on FeatureKeys.appOwnedVoucherTypes; the prod visibility evidence records app_owned_voucher_types = false. Under the access truth table a dark feature gets no public procedure, teaser or slug, so no section was written for it.

deliberatelyOmitted: Raw Tally/Postgres error strings; the guide describes the plain headlines the app shows and points at Technical details for support.
Any instruction to re-send or re-push a voucher — the screen offers no such control and doing it by hand would duplicate vouchers.
The 48-hour and 24-hour thresholds as numbers; the guide describes them as 'too long to be called normal' and 'more than a day old' so the page does not go stale if the constants move.
